messages.content: Follow the production contract exactly. Return valid JSON only.

AUTHORITATIVE SOURCE UNITS:
1. Amy cooks breakfast for Will and Amber.
2. A zombie breaks the kitchen door window; Amy gets Will and Amber into the basement and locks the door.
3. Amy retrieves her hidden pistol and katana and equips them.
4. The majority of the story is Amy fighting attacking zombies.
5. Amy kills the last zombie and the house is soaked in blood.
6. Amy lets Will and Amber out of the basement.

A chapter is a LARGE H3 refresh unit.
Use the FEWEST chapter boundaries that preserve major narrative phases.
Normal setup, inciting danger, protection of the children, arming, and the source-emphasized main fighting process are one continuous escalation unless a major reset occurs.
Explicit final-resolution/closure may begin a new chapter.

Return JSON with key new_chapter_after, an array of source-unit numbers. Do not include the final unit number.

We want fewest chapters preserving major narrative phases: normal setup, inciting danger, protection of children, arming, main fighting process continuous escalation unless reset; explicit final-resolution/closure may begin new chapter.

So likely two chapters? Setup (unit1), then rest as one big fight until resolution. But maybe we need a third for final closure after unit6. The instruction: "Explicit final-resolution/closure may begin a new chapter." So after unit5 or 6? Unit5 is last zombie killed, house soaked in blood; unit6 is Amy lets Will and Amber out of basement. That could be resolution.

So maybe chapters: Chapter1 includes units 1-4 (setup to arming). Then Chapter2 includes units 5-6 (fighting climax and closure). But we need new_chapter_after array with source-unit numbers after which a new chapter starts. So if first chapter ends at unit4, then new chapter begins after unit4. Also maybe second chapter ends at unit6? We don't include final unit number. So only one boundary: after unit4.

Thus output JSON: {"new_chapter_after":[4]}. Ensure valid JSON.
